   Indonesian police find empty server racks during raid on Megaspeed subsidiary
 Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
 PT Megaspeed International Indonesia operates out of the office of PT MettaDC Teknologi Indonesia, an Indonesian carrier-neutral data centre and sovereign AI infrastructure provider.
 ST PHOTO: WAHYUDI SOERIAATMADJA
 Wahyudi Soeriaatmadja
 Published   Nov 16, 2026, 01:15 PM
 Updated   Nov 16, 2026, 06:15 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise 中文 Indonesian police raided PT Megaspeed International Indonesia after an FBI request to trace Nvidia chips. They found empty server racks and no GPUs, suggesting the hardware was never installed.
 An official said most Nvidia hardware bought by Megaspeed may have gone through Indonesia and then to China, possibly by private jet. Police and Megaspeed officials gave little comment.
 The case adds pressure on Indonesia’s growing Nvidia-linked data centre plans in West Java and Batam. Some projects are still under construction, while Nvidia may also consider a US$4.5 billion Batam investment.
 AI generated
 JAKARTA – Indonesian police have searched the office of PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, the local arm of Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed International .
 The move, carried out earlier in 2026, was part of an inquiry requested by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to trace Nvidia chips bought by Megaspeed, according to a senior Indonesian government official, who requested anonymity as he is unauthorised to speak to the media.
 Officers from Indonesian National Police’s (INP) Criminal Investigation Department (Bareskrim) who inspected the premises found server racks at the site but no graphics processing units (GPUs), the source added. 
 The racks appeared never to have been unpacked or used, suggesting that the chips were never installed there.
 The raid, which was conducted before the recent Jensen Huang scandal , was the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case.
 The official alleged that most of the Nvidia hardware bought by Megaspeed entities was likely shipped to Indonesia. Investigators, he said, believe much of it was then sent to China, possibly by private jet.
 Inspector-General Untung Widyatmoko, head of INP’s International Relations Division, was asked by The Straits Times about the quantity of Nvidia GPUs that might have been shipped through Indonesia to China and whether FBI agents are in Indonesia working on the investigation. He declined to comment in a Nov 13 WhatsApp text message reply to ST.
 PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, a locally incorporated company owned by Singapore-based Megaspeed, has a listed address on the fifth floor of Cyber 1 building at No. 8 Jalan Kuningan Barat in South Jakarta. 
 ST checks on the office on Nov 13 found that PT Megaspeed is not on the building’s tenant list. A building receptionist told ST that PT Megaspeed instead operates out of the office of PT MettaDC Teknologi Indonesia (MettaDC), an Indonesian carrier-neutral data centre and sovereign AI infrastructure provider.
 An officer at MettaDC confirmed that Megaspeed uses its office, which is enclosed by tinted glass walls near the lift on that floor.
 The officer said Megaspeed also rents space in the Jababeka Industrial Estate in Cikarang, Bekasi, West Java. The facility is owned by PT HDC, a hyperscale data centre operator.
 Commissioner-General Asep Safrudin, head of Bareskrim, did not reply to ST’s query for comments about the case. He was also asked about the time frame of the police search on Megaspeed’s facilities in the Jababeka Industrial Estate, 45km east of Jakarta in the West Java province.
 Megaspeed is at the centre of a US national security probe. US officials suspect its former managing director, Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, of passing information to Beijing. Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12 .
 The Huang scandal has sparked calls for a clampdown on the export of cutting-edge US chips, which would complicate South-east Asia’s AI infrastructure build-out .
 The US Commerce Department is working on rules that would add Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore to a group of countries subject to export restrictions, The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov 15, citing sources.
 These rules would make it compulsory for companies exporting advanced chips such as Nvidia’s Blackwell series to those countries to get a licence that would prohibit Chinese customers from remotely accessing the computing power.
 On Nov 13, Malaysia’s Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry said it is working closely with Singapore and the US to strengthen safeguards against chip smuggling .
 Meanwhile, Singapore and the US have discussed the Megaspeed case at a senior-level meeting in Washington, with both countries committing to continue discussions on the matter, ST reported on Nov 14.
 In Indonesia, Nvidia-linked data centres, which are clustered in West Java and Batam, with Jakarta as the main hub, could come under greater scrutiny. Much of the capacity for these centres is still being planned or under construction.
 In Purwakarta, West Java, Raia Grid, a joint digital infrastructure venture of Indonesian investment conglomerate Arsari Group and telecommunications provider Indosat, is due to begin assembling 140 to 150 Nvidia GPUs in December.
 The company did not respond to a Nov 12 ST e-mail seeking a procurement update for their project.
 In Batam, Australian AI start-up Firmus and Singapore-based data centre operator DayOne are planning a 360 megawatt Nvidia AI Factory campus. It is set to receive up to 170,000 GPUs in 2027 and 2028, with initial operations targeted for 2027.
 Nvidia is also reportedly exploring a US$4.5 billion (S$5.8 billion) investment in Batam, but talks are ongoing and nothing is confirmed.
